The product rule for double summations states that

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{a}_{i}{b}_{j}={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{a}_{i}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{b}_{j}.
$$

So, using the product rule for double summations, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{20}{\sum }_{j=1}^{20}5{b}_{j}({a}_{i}-4) & ={\sum }_{j=1}^{20}5{b}_{j}{\sum }_{i=1}^{20}({a}_{i}-4).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the rules for single summations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{j=1}^{20}5{b}_{j}{\sum }_{i=1}^{20}({a}_{i}-4) & =(5{\sum }_{j=1}^{20}{b}_{j})\cdot ({\sum }_{i=1}^{20}{a}_{i}-{\sum }_{i=1}^{20}4) \\  & =(5{\sum }_{j=1}^{20}{b}_{j})\cdot ({\sum }_{i=1}^{20}{a}_{i}-4{\sum }_{i=1}^{20}1) \\  & =(5\cdot 18)\cdot (85-4\cdot 20) \\  & =(90)\cdot (85-80) \\  & =(90)\cdot (5) \\  & =450\end{aligned}
$$
